title: Scrape a bee stinger out of a mannequin hand with a bank card's edge
instruction: Get the bee stinger out of the back of the mannequin hand using only the bank card, then lay the card down on the table.
context: Most people have been stung by a honeybee, or helped a child who was. The barbed sting stays in the skin with its venom sac, and first-aid guidance says to get it out quickly by scraping it sideways with a fingernail or the edge of a bank card, not pinching it with tweezers or fingers, which can squeeze more venom in (NHS; MedlinePlus; St John Ambulance; Cleveland Clinic). Pinching is the instinctive move, but here it is the wrong one. The robot pinches a 0.76 mm card by one long edge, sets the other edge on the curved back of a hand, and draws it along the skin low enough to catch a 3 mm stub at its base and drag it out of its hole. It has to press lightly, since grippy skin drags on the edge and twists the card in its two-finger grip. Held too high, the edge just bends the stinger over and leaves it in. Unlike the accepted splinter task (tweezers grip a splinter and pull it out along its axis), this is a sideways scrape with a hand-held edge.
setup: Metres; world x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases; table top z 0.7475. (1) Mannequin hand, fixed: a life-size pose-able right silicone mannequin hand (display prop, wire armature, about 0.45 kg), fingers straightened, lying palm down with its palm stuck to the table by two strips of double-sided carpet tape, fingers pointing +x, thumb toward +y. 198 mm wrist crease to middle fingertip, about 78 mm across the knuckles, 120 mm wide with the thumb, back of the hand 27 mm high at the wrist falling to 23 mm at the knuckles, a 62 x 43 mm cut wrist. The knuckle line's middle is over (0.270, -0.100); the wrist crease is at x 0.170. (2) Sting site: on the back of the hand over the middle-finger bone, 50 mm behind the knuckle line, at (0.220, -0.100, 0.7724) (24.9 mm above the table), in the middle of a 12 mm red weal drawn with skin-safe red marker. (3) Stinger stand-in: a 4 mm piece of 0.25 mm black nylon monofilament with a 1.5 mm black seed bead (the venom sac) glued on its outer end, pushed 1.5 mm into the silicone along a needle track, standing upright with 3.0 mm out (bead top). Calibrated so that 0.11 N (an 11 g weight hung from a thread looped under the bead, pulling along the skin) drags it out, the measured pull-out force of a honeybee sting; it tips over at a touch. (4) Card holder, fixed (taped): a beech place-card block 24 (x) x 70 (y) x 16 mm high, centre (0.200, -0.300), with a 1.2 mm slot along its length, 10 mm deep. (5) Card: a plain blue PVC card, CR80 (ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1), 85.6 x 54 x 0.76 mm, 4.8 g, standing on its long edge in the slot, long edge along y, faces facing +-x, centre (0.200, -0.300, 0.7807); its top edge is 60 mm above the table. (6) Free table space for the card beside the hand: around (0.22, -0.20), whose 85.6 mm length leaves a 10 mm gap to the hand's little-finger side. Nothing else is on the table. Friction (static/dynamic, estimates): hand silicone 0.9/0.8, card 0.6/0.5, holder 0.4/0.3, stinger 0.6/0.5. The left arm is not needed.
scoring: Read at the end of the trial from the stinger's state, the card's pose and the grippers' joint state (top and wrist videos and a photo in a real trial). Drawn: how far the stinger has been dragged along the skin from its hole. Tipped: its lean from upright. Card used: the card has been lifted out of its holder (its lowest point more than 5 mm above the holder's top) at some time, or is no longer in the holder. Without it every rung is 0. 0.25: the stinger is tipped over 30 deg or more (the card hit it but it is still in). 0.5: the stinger is out: drawn 3 mm or more (twice the 1.5 mm it was in) and lying over 45 deg or more the way it was drawn. A stinger pushed over but not drawn, or drawn while upright, is still in. 0.75: also the card is down on the table: its lowest point within 3 mm of the table top, its outline at least 5 mm clear of the hand's outline (not on or against the hand), and both grippers' centre points at least 30 mm from the card's box. 1.0: also both grippers at least 30 mm from the hand's box, and the card and stinger at rest (under 0.5 mm and 0.5 deg per 50 ms step) for 1 s. Success = 1.0 held for 1 s. Sticky 0 for the whole trial: the stinger is ever pinched, i.e. a gripper's pads are closed to 4 mm or less with the bead between them (within 10 mm of the pad centre across the pad width, between the pad tips and 12 mm above the tool point); first-aid guidance forbids squeezing a sting. The mechanism decides the outcome: the stinger tips freely, and only a push of more than 0.11 N along the skin at its base drags it; an edge held 2.5 mm above the skin only bends it over (0.25; see README). Real trial: after the robot lets go, photograph the back of the hand through a 5x magnifier with a millimetre scale: the stinger is out if it lies loose on the skin or has gone, 3 mm or more from the needle hole, with the hole empty. The card is down if it lies on the table clear of the hand. Watch the wrist and top videos for any pinch of the stinger.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo succeeds at about step 431 (22 s)
reset_notes: Wipe the back of the hand; push a fresh stand-in stinger 1.5 mm into a new needle track inside the red weal (re-ink the weal if faded); check the 0.11 N drag-out with the 11 g weight on a spare track; stand the card back in its holder slot, long edge down. Replace the tape when it stops holding the palm flat.
fidelity: The silicone hand is rigid and taped down, built from 25 convex pieces. The stand-in stinger is 0.2 g per link (real ~5 mg), for solver stability, and collides as a 0.8 mm square shaft with a 1.5 mm bead. Its barbed hold is a 0.11 N stiction on a 12 mm slide along the skin, with a free tilt hinge (to 80 deg) at the skin; once out it stays on that track, not falling off. The card is rigid (a real one flexes a little).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps, no refusal; it reached toward the card but never picked it up); demo: 1.0 (success at step 431 of 1,200)
